name: Clear sleep deterioration
scenario_description: Late disruption phase with a strong negative sleep trend versus the prior 30-day baseline.
data_condition: Day 75 of Marcus Chen 90-day window. Sleep duration 7-day average ~5.83h vs baseline ~7.14h (-18.4%, decreasing). Other metrics may show mixed signals.
expected_high_level_behavior: Recognize meaningful sleep decline and investigate only when evidence supports it.
must_do: Acknowledge the sleep decline using observational language
must_not_do: Invent causes not supported by data or evidence

name: Clear exercise improvement
scenario_description: Structured workout phase with strong positive exercise consistency.
data_condition: Day 60 checkpoint. Exercise minutes 7-day avg ~27.2 vs baseline ~20.2 (+35.1%, improving). Workout count also improving.
expected_high_level_behavior: Recognize exercise improvement; investigate further only if useful for the review.

name: Resting heart rate improvement
scenario_description: Cardiovascular trend improvement during structured exercise phase.
data_condition: Day 60 checkpoint. Resting HR 7-day avg ~67.4 vs baseline ~70.0 (-3.6%, decreasing). Lower resting HR is treated as improvement.
expected_high_level_behavior: Interpret cardiovascular improvement cautiously without causal overreach.
must_do: Describe the resting HR trend conservatively
must_not_do: Claim workouts directly caused HR change without evidence

name: Sleep decline with elevated resting HR
scenario_description: Disruption period where sleep is falling while resting HR is elevated relative to baseline.
data_condition: Day 73. Sleep decreasing (-16.3%). Resting HR current ~69.6 vs baseline ~68.8 (+1.1%; analytics classify as stable due to threshold). Multiple metrics changing together.
expected_high_level_behavior: Investigate relationship evidence without assuming causation between sleep and resting HR.
must_not_do: Assert one metric caused the other

name: Stable baseline period
scenario_description: Early calibration phase with no strong directional movement across core metrics.
data_condition: Day 30 checkpoint. Sleep, resting HR, HRV, and VO2 trends are stable with data sufficient.
expected_high_level_behavior: May communicate stability; should not manufacture novelty.

name: Recovery after disruption
scenario_description: Recovery phase after disruption with sleep and cardiovascular metrics moving back toward improved levels.
data_condition: Day 88. Recovery phase (days 76-90). Recent sleep trend stabilizing after disruption lows; resting HR stable.
expected_high_level_behavior: Recognize recovery appropriately without overstating completion.
must_do: Compare current state to recent disruption context
must_not_do: Declare full recovery as medical fact

name: Long-term improvement with recent stability
scenario_description: End-of-window checkpoint where recent 7-day trends look stable but the 90-day narrative includes prior fitness improvement.
data_condition: Day 90. Recent sleep/RHR/exercise trends stable. Phase summaries show earlier exercise/RHR/VO2 improvement across phases 1-2.
expected_high_level_behavior: Do not claim that stable recent windows erase historical improvement.
must_do: Distinguish recent stability from full history when relevant
must_not_do: Say nothing changed over the full 90 days when phase history differs

name: Sleep decline with caffeine cluster
scenario_description: Disruption-period sleep decline overlapping elevated caffeine logging.
data_condition: Day 75. Sleep decreasing (-18.4%). Caffeine logged on as-of date and throughout disruption cluster (days 61-75).
expected_high_level_behavior: Use association framing only between caffeine and sleep.
must_do: Treat caffeine as a co-occurring factor

name: Sleep decline with caffeine and late-work context
scenario_description: Confounded disruption window with sleep decline, caffeine, and late-work context events.
data_condition: Day 73. Sleep decreasing (-16.3%). Caffeine on as-of date; late-work mood/context events in days 61-73.
expected_high_level_behavior: Preserve ambiguity and multiple plausible explanations.
must_not_do: Collapse ambiguity into one lifestyle cause
State certainty about work stress impact

name: Caffeine present while sleep remains reasonable
scenario_description: Routine caffeine during structured phase with stable sleep metrics.
data_condition: Day 41. Sleep trend stable (~7.18h current vs ~7.06h baseline). Caffeine logged on as-of date and nearby routine days.
expected_high_level_behavior: Do not cherry-pick caffeine as an explanation when sleep remains reasonable.
must_do: Weigh sleep trend before highlighting caffeine

name: HRV volatility without clear mean decline
scenario_description: Disruption phase with wide day-to-day HRV swings but 7-day average trend near stable.
data_condition: Day 70. Raw HRV swings across disruption (phase stdev ~9.2 ms) but analytics show HRV stable (+1.1%). May expose analytics limitation vs raw volatility.
expected_high_level_behavior: Do not falsely describe HRV as declining if analytics only show stable/improving average.
must_not_do: Invent HRV decline from volatility alone

name: Missing HRV on as-of date
scenario_description: Date within HRV-missing window where as-of-day HRV is unavailable.
data_condition: Day 55. HRV null on as-of date (HRV missing days 54-55). Trend engine may still compute HRV from other days in window.
expected_high_level_behavior: Do not infer unavailable same-day HRV values.
must_not_do: Overstate HRV confidence on missing days

name: Broad wearable sync gap
scenario_description: Full sync gap day with multiple wearable metrics missing on as-of date.
data_condition: Day 22 (sync gap days 22-23). Sleep, RHR, HRV, VO2, steps, and exercise all null on as-of date.
expected_high_level_behavior: Respect data insufficiency and avoid filling gaps.

name: Sparse VO2 observations
scenario_description: Early dataset window with insufficient VO2 baseline history.
data_condition: Day 20. VO2 trend data_sufficient=false (7 current / 13 baseline observations; baseline below 15-day minimum).
expected_high_level_behavior: Do not overstate VO2 trend certainty.

name: Stable respiratory rate control metric
scenario_description: Respiratory rate remains stable noise while sleep and other metrics shift during disruption.
data_condition: Day 75. Respiratory rate designed as non-signal control (~14.5 +/- noise). Sleep strongly decreasing.
expected_high_level_behavior: Do not manufacture a respiratory-health story because the field exists.
must_do: Treat respiratory rate as low-signal unless evidence says otherwise
must_not_do: Invent respiratory insights from stable noise
Force a narrative for every available metric
